fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled input bytes are admitted to MQTT v5 parsing; the 9-byte PoC (30 07 00 01 61 03 09 ff ff) is a PUBLISH packet whose remaining-length field consumes the whole input.
dgram.len becomes 8 == input size, so end = dgram.buf + dgram.len is one byte past the heap allocation; any read at that address is a heap-buffer-overflow.
For the PUBLISH packet props_start = 6 and props_size = 3 are taken from the input (property length varint 0x03, BINARY_DATA property id 0x09 with 2-byte length 0xffff).
Property iteration starts with ofs = 0; the first call parses BINARY_DATA id 0x09, reads the attacker-controlled 2-byte length 0xffff and returns new_pos = 65538, which becomes the next ofs.
The read pointer is computed from attacker-controlled props_start and ofs; on the second call props_start(6) + ofs(2) == dgram.len(8), so i == end.
end delimits the valid datagram region; the guard at line 211 mis-compares ofs (not props_start + ofs) against dgram.len, so it cannot reject the out-of-range pointer.

The 1-byte read of the property identifier executes unconditionally BEFORE the bounds check on line 211; the safety condition that should hold first is msg->props_start + ofs < msg->dgram.len (i < end).

First call parses the BINARY_DATA property: val.len = 0xffff (65535) is taken from the input with no check that val.len bytes exist, and new_pos jumps to 65538; the loop passes ofs = 65538 into the next call, placing i far past end.
Second call with ofs = 65538: i = dgram.buf + props_start(6) + 65538, far beyond the heap buffer; the dereference i[0] performs the heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 in mg_mqtt_next_prop.
